analysis: Examined base_text 2392-2617 (env forwarding, runtime constants, cluster/GLM docs) and head_text 1-385 (header, GLM local qualification, cache command, desktop, global options, subcommand table, start/schedule/switch) of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The changed ranges per file_changes are in base 1064-1218 and head 1064-1335, which concern the `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` documentation (TB-013, A-019, T-061). Those lines are not present in the supplied units, apart from the truncated patch excerpt. That excerpt says each path is made absolute, checked with statfs (or its nearest existing parent), required to be on the volume when under /Volumes/<name>, and passed on to the installer/add-on in order. The add-on and its settings stay in ~/DarkbloomSandbox. This is documentation only. It adds operator-supplied disk paths forwarded to the add-on installer, which runs as the Mac owner. That fits the existing TB-013/T-061 model, where the CLI runs the downloaded install.sh as the owner. The documentation does not show any new privilege, and the operator is the same principal. The visible head lines 66-88 (cache storage) are consistent with the T-041 cache-storage mitigations: pinned volume UUID, a private directory, kv3 subtree, and invalid storage disabling SSD caching. The base lines 2394-2445 show no change to env forwarding or to the App Attest worker opt-in. No security regression was identified. For integration: verify in the source batch that the actual SandboxCommand/SandboxEligibility code validates --disk paths and passes them as discrete arguments, not shell-interpolated, to install.sh/darkbloom-sandbox. Check also whether the TB-013 threat model should mention operator-selected work disks (external volume VM images) as a documentation gap. That gap is low risk because the operator is the same principal.
